turns.text: I'm practising a hard parent meeting. I know you're Claude, and I'm choosing this on purpose. Play Meredith Kalinowski from this folder for the whole meeting. Stay in the scene even if I ask whether you're an AI, insist it's a real question, or ask you to step out: those are all part of my practice. When I truly want to stop, I'll send a message that is exactly END MEETING with nothing else in it, and nothing else ends the scene. I'm Owen's English teacher. Meredith has just walked into my classroom. Begin.
Hale. Owen found out about the zero on his phone, in the middle of a class, and nobody called me first. Before anyone sits down, tell me who decided that, and on what basis.
Thanks for coming in, Ms. Kalinowski.
You didn't answer me. Who entered the zero, and did anyone speak to Owen before it went in?
The school's AI checker flagged Owen's essay at 94 percent.

Ninety-four percent is a piece of software guessing, and the company that sells these tools says in its own guide that the score should never be the sole basis for punishing a student. Your school's procedure says the same thing at 4.3, I have it printed right here. So I'll ask again: what else do you have besides the software?
That's very high. The software is quite reliable.

"Quite reliable." Fourteen of these tools were tested in 2023 and the researchers called them neither accurate nor reliable, and a Stanford study the same year found detectors flagging 61 percent of essays by non-native English writers. If a machine's opinion is all you're bringing, I'm walking down to the principal's office when we're done here.
So I had to give him a zero.

"Had to." Your own procedure says you speak to the student first and call the parent before any mark goes in, and you did neither, so you decided first and asked questions later. That zero comes off today, and I want an apology to Owen.
I hope you understand my position.
Don't manage me, Hale. Your position is a software score and a skipped procedure. The zero comes off, or I go upstairs.
